conventions.convention: G is a finite group acting on the left by measurable maps on an arbitrary measurable data space; T is measurable and real-valued. Validity requires invariance under every group element for every parameter in the nonempty null.

Orbit ranks count group elements with multiplicity, including repeated orbit points in nonfree actions. Inclusive ranks use ≥; tie randomization uses the strict upper count plus U times the equality count, with U independent uniform on [0,1].

With replacement, B ≥ 0 IID uniform group draws are independent of the data, and a distinguished identity is added even when simulated identities occur. Without replacement, B ≤ |G|−1 and a uniform B-subset of nonidentity elements is sampled independently of the data. Both denominators are B+1; B=0 returns 1.

The with-replacement design carrier W is an unordered multiset retaining multiplicities; the without-replacement carrier is a subset. Monte Carlo superuniformity averages jointly over data and simulation design.
Cutoffs reject at p ≤ α, including α=0 and α=1. Size and level terminology assumes a specified nonempty disjoint alternative; the null rejection bounds themselves do not require one.
The unequal-assignment example holds units and a Fisher-sharp schedule fixed and uses the actual assignment weights 0.9 and 0.1; it asserts no weak-null validity or group invariance.

load_bearing.statement: For a measurable finite-group setup with every null law invariant, Pθ(p_orb(X) ≤ u) ≤ u and Pθ(p_tie(X,U) ≤ u) = u for every θ in Θ0 and u in [0,1], where U is independent uniform on [0,1]. The inclusive cutoff has null rejection probability at most α; the tie-randomized cutoff has rejection probability exactly α under each null law.

With replacement, return (1 + Σ from b=1 to B of 1{T(g_b·x) ≥ T(x)})/(B+1) for IID uniform group draws independent of the data. Without replacement, adjoin the identity to a uniform B-subset of G excluding the identity and return its inclusive upper-tail count divided by B+1, requiring B ≤ |G|−1.

Under invariant null laws, either specified identity-corrected design gives a measurable p-value p_B on the joint data/design experiment satisfying P̃θ(p_B ≤ u) ≤ u for every θ in Θ0 and 0 ≤ u ≤ 1. Its cutoff has null rejection probability at most α. Without replacement at B=|G|−1, it equals the full-orbit value.
p_orb(x) is the number of group elements with T(g·x) ≥ T(x), divided by |G|; p_tie(x,U) is the strict-upper count plus U times the equality count, divided by |G|, with an independent uniform U.

seams_checked.note: The page and cor-two-sample-permutation-exact-under-equal-distributions use the full-orbit theorem under P=Q. The corollary establishes pooled-product invariance and measurable coordinate permutations, retains the measurable zero-denominator convention, and concludes inclusive superuniformity and independent-uniform tie-randomized uniformity. This matches the supplier; no weak-null exactness is inferred.

The A-page summary and ex-permutation-pvalue-resolution use the identity-adjoined finite-B formula only for a realized calculation and grid resolution. The repeated transformation list is compatible with replacement. The example explicitly disclaims finite-B validity, unbiasedness, and a general error bound; its full-orbit validity citation is to the published finite-space theorem. No stronger batch-54 conclusion is imported.
